decisions.reason: As a newly launched product with its own presentation page and clear fit to the firm's drainage-system engineering base, it is too early to abandon while uncertainty is still high and the option value remains meaningful.

A floor-level shower drainage system sits directly in the firm's strategic direction toward accessible, low-profile bathroom drainage, so management would keep the option open after only one year on the market.

This designer shower drainage product matches the firm's design-conscious positioning and received standalone website emphasis, so the prudent choice is to continue learning from the market rather than exit early.
The integrated-slope shower element strongly complements the firm's installation-ease and renovation value proposition, and one year of market exposure is not enough to justify abandonment.
The backflow-protected basement floor drain addresses a specific customer problem, was prominently launched on its own page, and should be retained while demand and adoption become clearer.

Compared with the other launches, the air-admittance valve appears less central to the firm's main differentiation and only weakly emphasized, so with several stronger options in hand management would reallocate resources away from it.
